2. The short facts relating for disposal of the rule are that, the opposite party obtained decree on 27-3-2000 in Civil Case No.784 of the Federal Court of First Instance, Abu Dhabi City, United Arab Emirates and put the said decree into execution in the Court of Joint District Judge, Dhaka through Money Execution Case No. 2 of 2004. The petitioner filed application for rejection of the Money Execution case as per provisions of Order VII Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The said application was rejected by the learned Joint District judge Dhaka by order No.14 dated 28-11-2004. The petitioner, thereafter, filed another application for the same relief. By the order dated 14-7-2005 the learned Joint District judge rejected the said application. Against which the petitioner moved before the learned District Judge in Civil Revision No. 406 of 2005. The learned District Judge summarily rejected the same on 24-8-2005. 

 3. Mr Md Mustafizur Rahman Khan, learned Advocate, appearing for the petitioner, submits that, section 44A(i) of the Code of Civil Procedure after amendment in 2003, stand for execution of any decree passed by a Court which has no reciprocating territory of Bangladesh Court as such, decree obtained in such country is unexcitable in Bangladesh. Learned Advocate on referring to the application filed by the petitioner for reconsideration of earlier order before the learned Joint District Judge referred to paragraph 8 of the said application where the petitioner placed before the Court as "according to mandatory provisions and settled principle of law related to Section 44A(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, the judgment and decree of Abu Dhabi Court, UAE are not executable in Bangladesh in any manner whatsoever in any Court as the UAE is not being or of a Court of a "Reciprocating Territory" and, as such, the present execution case being not maintainable under the said Section 44A(1) of CPC is liable to be rejected with cost." 

 4. Learned Advocate further submits that, second application filed by the petitioner for the same relief before the learned joint district Judge in not any way stand as bar in the revision before the learned Judge for not paying any relief against the refusal of 1st application and cannot stopped the learned district Judge in giving relief to the petitioner as the decree cannot be executable in Bangladesh as law does not permit so, the Courts below committed gross illegality in not considering the application under Order VII Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 5. The question is very limited as whether UAE is reciprocating territory of Bangladesh and if not, then according so Section 44A of the Code of Civil Procedure whether the decree . can be executable in Bangladesh. 

 7. It appears from the judgment of the Courts below that the learned Judges did not consider whether United Arab Emirates in a reciprocating territory of Bangladesh and if so, whether any notification as required under law, was published in the official gazette as per provision of law, (under Section 44A) as notification to that effect is to be published year to year. Bangladesh and India declared to be 'Reciprocating Territory' by simultaneous gazette notification dated 1-7-76 and 1-2-76 respectively. The opposite party decree holder did not produce any paper before the Courts below to that effect as such, we are of the view that the Court below acted illegally in rejecting the application filed by the petitioner. 

 9. The foremost question is whether decree holder Janata Bank filed the execution case before the learned Joint District Judge legally. It is an admitted fact the decree holder Janata Bank is a financial institute within the meaning of Section 2 of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003, Act VII of 2003 and this Ain provides realization of decreetal amount, as such, the execution case, as per provision of law, ought to be filed before Artha Rin Adalat, not before Joint District Judge. It may be, as per sub-Section 4 of the AM, Joint District Judge constitute Artha Rin Adalat, but unless there be a notification through gazette, Joint Districtinnot act as Artha Rin Adalat. 

 "Where a certified copy of a decree of any of the superior Courts of the United Kingdom or any reciprocating territory has been filed in a District Court, the decree may be executed in Bangladesh as if it has been passed by the District Court. " 

 11. Together with the certified copy of the decree, a certificate shall be filed from such superior Court stating the extend, if any, to which the decree has been satisfied or adjusted and such certificate shall, for the purposes of proceedings under this section, be conclusive proof of the extend of such satisfaction or adjustment. 

 12. The provisions of section 47 shall as from filing of the certified copy of the decree apply to the proceedings of a District Court executing a decree under this section, and (deemed to be excluded as section 47 has been omitted by amendment) the District Court shall refuse execution of any such decree, if it is shown to the satisfaction of the Court that the decree falls within any of the exceptions specified in clauses (a) to (f) of section 13" 

 13. District Court mentioned means only the Court of District Judge and certified copy of the decree shall be filed in the Court of District Judge for its execution, not to Joint District Judge. There is a difference between District Court and District Judge. District Court means the principal civil Court of a district and District Judge means the Judge of a principal civil Court, not to any one inferior. When execution of a foreign decree is required, if must filed before the District Judge, no to any other Judge. Here, we may refer to the decision of Sonali Bank vs Abidur Rahman wherein it is held as— 

 "'The District Court' mentioned in Section 44A(I) of the Code means only the Court of District Judge. In other words, the certified copy of decree under Section 44A(I) of the Code must be filed in the Court of District Judge."
